summary: JClaw guards its gates with eight 'conformance' tests that read the build script, the runner's discovery rule and the source tree directly, each with a count floor so a scan that matches nothing cannot pass. We already have the strongest form of most of this (chaosGate pins the plant count by READING the runner's constant; claimcheck floors its corpus at >1600/>350; configTwins pins 36 + a deny-list). Four real holes remain, all of the 'suite silently runs less than you think' family, and three are one-to-ten-line fixes: (1) vitest allows `it.only` locally by default, so a focused test shrinks a file to one test and the pre-commit stays green (MEASURED: `Tests 1 passed | 1 skipped`); (2) ten independent `existsSync` skip-guards let any one renamed reference file silently switch off a byte-check suite; (3) a `.spec.ts` or `src/*.test.ts` file is never collected because our include glob is narrower than vitest's default and nothing compares `vitest list` to the tree; (4) agent-harness's only documented self-check, `node --test 'harness/**/*.test.mjs'`, exits 0 with `# tests 0` on Node 26.8.1 when the glob matches nothing (MEASURED), and that repo has no hook, no count pin and a README/RESUME_HERE that disagree on the test count (43 vs 24). Two lesser items: `core.hooksPath` is verified nowhere (a fresh clone has no gate), and the hook tests the working tree, not the index. One acknowledged drift: SSHD's chaosLib.ts and agent-harness's chaosLib.mjs are two copies of one rule, and RESUME_HERE already owes the port.

candidates.pattern: Fail the suite on a focused test (`it.only` / `describe.only`) in every environment, not only under CI
candidates.failurePrevented: A session debugs with `it.only`, forgets it, commits: vitest runs ONE test in that file, reports the rest as skipped, exits 0, and the pre-commit gate passes. Because the hook also exits 0 whenever `$CI` is set, there is no environment on this machine where vitest's own CI guard would ever fire.
candidates.jclawEvidence: test/TestDiscoveryConformanceTest.java:13 "Guards the one way this suite can lie: silently running nothing (JCLAW-1176)." — same family (a suite that reports green over tests it never ran). JClaw's runner cannot express `.only`; the lesson transfers as the vitest-specific switch.
candidates.builtAndExercised: JClaw: commit 5cd087a1 2026-09-10 "test(discovery): fail the build on a test class the runner never reaches (JCLAW-1176)"; header line 18 names the real victim: "MultiImageVideoAdapterTest sat that way with two live test methods until this check found it". OUR side MEASURED in the scratchpad with SSHD's own vitest 4.1.10: default run of a file with `it.only` → `Tests 1 passed | 1 skipped (2)`, `Test Files 1 passed (1)`; with `--allowOnly=false` → `FAIL t/a.test.mjs > focused  Error: [Vitest] Unexpected .only modifier`.
candidates.ourEvidence: vite.config.ts is 8 lines: `test: { include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts'], environment: 'node' }` — no `allowOnly`. `grep -rn 'allowOnly\|passWithNoTests\|no-focused-tests\|eslint-plugin-vitest' vite.config.ts eslint.config.mjs package.json tests` → empty. `grep -rnE '\b(it|test|describe)\.(only)\(' tests --include='*.ts'` → 0 hits today (so nothing is broken now; nothing would catch it tomorrow). Context7 /vitest-dev/vitest defaults.ts: `allowOnly: !isCI`. .githooks/pre-commit:12 `[ -n "$CI" ] && exit 0` — the hook never runs under CI, so vitest's CI guard is unreachable here.
candidates.proposal: vite.config.ts, one line inside `test: {}`: `allowOnly: false, // a forgotten it.only shrinks a file to one test and the gate stays green (measured 2026-09-14)`. Optionally one chaos plant in tests/*.plants.ts that inserts `.only` into a test and names that file — but the plant harness requires a FAILED test, which this produces, so it fits.
candidates.doneCriterion: Add `it.only` to any test in tests/, run `npx vitest run` → exit non-zero with `Unexpected .only modifier`; remove it → green with the same total as before (RESUME_HERE: 1631).
candidates.cost: 1 line; 0 tokens per turn; 0 dependencies; ~2 min.
candidates.why: Smallest possible change that closes a measured fail-open; nothing else in the toolchain (no vitest eslint plugin, no CI) can see it.

candidates.pattern: A skip-guarded suite must fail, not skip, when the thing it is guarded on is present but the guard's own probe drifted — 'a checker switched off' must go red
candidates.failurePrevented: Ten byte-check suites are each guarded by their own `existsSync(<one specific file>)`. Rename or move one reference file (or the whole tree) and that suite skips; vitest prints `N skipped` on the Tests line, the pre-commit prints that line and still commits. The suite reads green with a transcription gate switched off. JClaw's AGENTS.md names the mirror image for its frontend ("in a fresh worktree run nuxi prepare first or the suite false-REDs with zero tests"); ours false-GREENs, the worse direction.
candidates.jclawEvidence: test/NullnessGateConformanceTest.java:17-19 "nothing in the suite would notice the gate being switched off, downgraded to a warning, or left behind by a new subpackage"; :35-37 SILENT_SWITCH_OFFS list; test/ResourceLeakGateConformanceTest.java:94-95 "A hierarchy walk that silently stopped resolving would pass this test on an empty set." + `assertTrue(scanned.size() >= 7, ...)`.
candidates.builtAndExercised: JClaw: commit 88b142ee 2026-09-06 "test(gates): close the silent switch-offs the conformance tests could not see (JCLAW-1149, JCLAW-1156, ...)" — the second iteration, i.e. the first version of these guards was itself found fail-open and closed.
candidates.ourEvidence: `grep -rnE 'const (HAVE_SOURCE|HAVE_BINDATA|hasReference) =' tests` → 10 definitions in 10 files, each on a DIFFERENT file (ogAiData.test.ts:154 `existsSync(path.join(SCRIPTS, 'NPCManager.as'))`, npcTree.test.ts:33 `'NPC.as'`, ogItemData.test.ts:221 `ITEMDATA`, composePose.test.ts:228 `BINDATA`, ...). Only claimcheck.test.ts:309-316 makes the skip loud (`process.stdout.write('[claimcheck] SKIPPED: ... This is not a pass.')`) and it only writes; nothing FAILS. .githooks/pre-commit:39-41 greps the `Tests` line and prints it — no assertion on `skipped`. RESUME_HERE.md:19 records the healthy shape `Tests 1631 passed (1631)` (no skipped segment). `reference/decompiled/shs3_android_payload/scripts` exists on this machine (ls → yes), so today 0 skip.
candidates.proposal: .githooks/pre-commit, inside `run_step` after the tests grep (4 lines): `if [ "$1" = tests ] && [ -d reference/decompiled/shs3_android_payload/scripts ] && grep -qE '^ *Tests .*skipped' "$log"; then printf '❌ tests SKIPPED with reference/ present — a byte-check guard drifted. Not a pass.\n'; exit 1; fi`. (With gate-guards-1 in place `.only` is caught earlier; this catches the ten skipIf guards, which `.only` does not cover.) Do NOT consolidate the ten `existsSync`s into one constant — each guards a different file on purpose; the hook-level assertion is the one place that sees them all.
candidates.doneCriterion: Chaos-style check by hand: edit tests/ogItemData.test.ts:221 to point ITEMDATA at a bogus path, stage a trivial .ts change, `git commit` → refused with 'tests SKIPPED with reference/ present'; revert → commit proceeds and the printed line has no `skipped`.
candidates.cost: 4 lines of sh; 0 per-turn tokens; ~10 min including the by-hand red/green.
candidates.why: JClaw asserts the checker's wiring from inside a test; for us the cheapest single point that sees every skip is the hook's already-parsed summary line. A test cannot read its own run's skip count.

candidates.pattern: Every file that declares tests must be one the runner collects — compare the runner's discovery against the tree, with a floor so an empty scan cannot pass
candidates.failurePrevented: A session writes `tests/npcSlice4.spec.ts` or `src/core/x.test.ts` (both are vitest's DEFAULT spellings; many skills/templates use `.spec.ts`). Our include is the narrower `tests/**/*.test.ts`, so the file compiles, is linted, and never runs; the suite is green. vitest's `passWithNoTests: false` only covers the case where ZERO files match.
candidates.jclawEvidence: test/TestDiscoveryConformanceTest.java:15-19 "A plain JUnit class under test/ compiles, is never executed, and the suite still reports green — so the failure mode is an absence, which no assertion inside that class can ever report."; :64 `assertTrue(examined > 400, "the scan reached only " + examined + " files — it is not measuring the suite")`.
candidates.builtAndExercised: JClaw: commit 5cd087a1 2026-09-10; AGENTS.md:31 "A class that extends neither play.test.UnitTest nor FunctionalTest never runs; TestDiscoveryConformanceTest now fails the build on one, so it no longer needs watching by hand." The predicate has its own shape test (`thePredicateNamesTheShapeItIsLookingFor`).
candidates.ourEvidence: `find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o \( -name '*.test.ts' -o -name '*.spec.ts' -o -name '*.test.mts' -o -name '*.test.js' \) -print | grep -v '^./tests/'` → nothing (no orphan today). tests/chaosGate.test.ts:118-125 already shells `npx vitest list --filesOnly` but only asserts `.plants.ts` is NOT in it — the inverse direction (everything that should be collected IS) is nowhere. tests/utils/npcHarness.ts:36 relies on the narrow include by comment only: "NOT collected as a suite: vite.config.ts sets include: ['tests/**\/*.test.ts']".
candidates.proposal: tests/chaosGate.test.ts (it already has the `vitest list --filesOnly` call and the ROOT): one more `it`: build `declared` = every `git ls-files` path under tests/ or src/ whose text matches `/^\s*(describe|it|test)(\.each)?\(/m` and is not in tests/utils/ or tests/fixtures/; assert `declared ⊆ collected` and `collected.length >= 80` (83 files today) so a parser that matches nothing cannot pass.
candidates.doneCriterion: Create tests/probe.spec.ts containing one `it(...)` → the new test fails naming `tests/probe.spec.ts`; rename to `.test.ts` → passes. The floor: temporarily set the include glob to `tests/zz/**` → the test fails on the floor, not vacuously.
candidates.cost: ~12 lines in an existing file; ~1 s added to the suite (one more `vitest list` — reuse the existing call's output); 0 per-turn tokens.
candidates.why: Exact JClaw shape, but reuse the discovery call chaosGate already makes rather than a new file; the narrow include is a deliberate choice (keeps plants and helpers out) so guard it instead of widening it.

candidates.pattern: The harness repo's own test command must fail on zero tests and pin a floor — `node --test <glob>` passes when the glob matches nothing
candidates.failurePrevented: agent-harness is PUBLIC and its only documented verification is `node --test 'harness/**/*.test.mjs'`. Move a test file, misquote the glob, or run from the wrong directory and Node reports `# tests 0`, `# fail 0`, exit 0 — 'all tests pass'. There is no package.json, no hook, no count pin in that repo, and its two docs already disagree on the count.
candidates.jclawEvidence: test/TestDiscoveryConformanceTest.java:63-64 "A scan that silently matched nothing would report the same empty list as a clean tree." / `assertTrue(examined > 400, ...)`; test/SidecarDefaultPortsConformanceTest.java:28-29 "a regex that silently stopped matching must not pass by finding none" + `KNOWN_MANAGERS = 7`; AGENTS.md:32 "Never pipe the suite (`| tail` returns tail's exit code); redirect to a file".
candidates.builtAndExercised: JClaw: the floor idiom appears in 4 of the 8 files read (TestDiscovery >400, ResourceLeak >=7 and >=20, SpaBuildInputs KNOWN_ESCAPING_IMPORTS=14, SidecarDefaultPorts KNOWN_MANAGERS=7), all committed and running in `play autotest`. OUR side MEASURED: `node --test 'zz-nope/**/*.test.mjs'` on Node v26.8.1 → exit 0, tap summary `# tests 0 / # pass 0 / # fail 0`; an explicit missing FILE (`node --test /tmp/zz-nope.test.mjs`) → exit 1. So the glob form is the fail-open one.
candidates.ourEvidence: agent-harness/harness/README.md:130 "**Check it yourself:** `node --test 'harness/**/*.test.mjs'` — 43 tests."; agent-harness/RESUME_HERE.md:9 "VERIFY: `node --test harness/` → 24 pass" (two numbers for one suite); `ls agent-harness` → no package.json; `ls agent-harness/.githooks` → does not exist; `grep -hoE '^\s*test\(' harness/*/*.test.mjs | wc -l` → 41 (loops/each not counted — not reconciled with 43). SSHD is fine on this axis: vitest's `passWithNoTests` defaults false and chaosLib.baselineIsGreen requires `passed > 0` (scripts/gates/chaosLib.ts:75-78).
candidates.proposal: agent-harness/harness/test.sh (≈8 lines, committed, referenced from README and RESUME_HERE in place of the bare command): `node --test --test-reporter=tap 'harness/**/*.test.mjs' > "$log" 2>&1; code=$?`; then `grep -q '^# fail 0$' "$log"` and `n=$(sed -n 's/^# tests //p' "$log")`, `[ "$n" -ge 40 ]` else print the summary block and exit 1. Node's own `--test-reporter=tap` is used because the spec reporter on Node 26 prints `ℹ tests` (memory: 'Node 26 spec reporter hid 3 chaos results'). Also fix RESUME_HERE.md:9 to the measured count.
candidates.doneCriterion: `sh harness/test.sh` → prints `# tests 4x` and exits 0; `sh harness/test.sh` after `mv harness/chaos/chaosLib.test.mjs /tmp/` → exits 1 on the floor (restore). Running it from a wrong cwd → exits 1, never 0.
candidates.cost: ~8 lines of sh + 2 doc lines; 0 dependencies (the repo's whole point); ~15 min.
candidates.why: The harness that teaches 'a probe whose parser matched nothing has not passed' (harness/README.md rule 6) currently verifies itself with exactly such a probe. Floor + fail-closed, not an exact pin, so adding tests does not churn it (JClaw's choice too).

candidates.pattern: Gate-wiring conformance: a test that reads the hook and the checker configs with comments stripped and asserts the gate is wired, on, and at error severity — including that git is actually pointed at the hook
candidates.failurePrevented: Three silent switch-offs: (a) a fresh clone or a new machine has no `core.hooksPath`, so `.githooks/pre-commit` never fires and every commit is ungated (JClaw: "hooks silently don't fire"); (b) one of the hook's three commands set to `""` (the file itself advertises `Leave one "" to skip that step`), so a step is disabled with the tick still printed for the others; (c) a checker downgraded — `allowOnly` re-added as true, `strict` flipped, `strictTypeChecked` swapped for `recommended`, the eslint `ignores` list widened — with no test noticing.
candidates.jclawEvidence: test/NullnessGateConformanceTest.java:20-22 "These assertions read build.gradle.kts and the package-info.java files directly, which is the only way to make those three regressions fail a test run rather than a later push."; :67-68 `check("NullAway", CheckSeverity.ERROR)` "a warning nobody reads is not a gate"; test/ResourceLeakGateConformanceTest.java:50-53 `withoutComments` "Comments are where a required token survives after the code that needed it is gone."; AGENTS.md:85 "Without the setup, hooks silently don't fire and /deploy fails on the github push."
candidates.builtAndExercised: JClaw: commits b87f4384 / 19d873dc 2026-09-05/06 (gates added with their conformance tests in the same change) and 88b142ee 2026-09-06 (the switch-off deny-list added after the first version was found blind). hooksPath is handled by `./jclaw.sh setup` (AGENTS.md:80-85), a setup step, not a test.
candidates.ourEvidence: `git config core.hooksPath` in SSHD → `.githooks` (wired on THIS machine only); `grep -rn hooksPath CLAUDE.md RESUME_HERE.md docs/research/HARNESS.md src/*/CLAUDE.md` → nothing; `grep -rnE 'pre-commit|hooksPath|tsconfig|eslint\.config|vite\.config|package\.json' tests scripts --include='*.ts'` → only comments (chaosGate.test.ts:4, claimcheck.test.ts:2,12, npcHarness.ts:36) — no test reads any of these files. .githooks/pre-commit:3 "Leave one "" to skip that step." Per-line switch-offs are not a live problem: `grep -rnE 'eslint-disable|@ts-ignore|@ts-expect-error|@ts-nocheck' src tests scripts --include='*.ts'` → 1 hit, with a reason (tests/progression.test.ts:219).
candidates.proposal: tests/gateWiring.test.ts, ~30 lines, four `it`s, each reading the file via a tiny `withoutComments` (strip `/*…*/`, `//…`, `#…` for sh): (1) `execFileSync('git',['config','core.hooksPath'])` trims to `.githooks` and `.githooks/pre-commit` is executable (`statSync(...).mode & 0o111`); (2) the hook's `BUILD_CMD=`, `TEST_CMD=`, `LINT_CMD=` are each non-empty and TEST_CMD contains `vitest run`; (3) vite.config.ts contains `allowOnly: false` and `include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']`; (4) tsconfig.json has `"strict": true` and eslint.config.mjs contains `strictTypeChecked` and its `ignores` array equals the four entries it has today. Assert positives with comments stripped; skip JClaw's negative string blacklist (see antiPattern 2).
candidates.doneCriterion: `git config --unset core.hooksPath && npx vitest run tests/gateWiring.test.ts` → red naming hooksPath; `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` → green. Set `LINT_CMD=""` in the hook → red; restore → green. All four assertions watched red once by hand before commit (ship-bar rule 3).
candidates.cost: ~30 lines, one new test file, +4 tests, <50 ms; 0 per-turn tokens; ~25 min including the red-first pass.
candidates.why: Insurance, not a bleeding wound (the tree has one annotated `@ts-expect-error` and no `.only`), but each assertion is a line, the hooksPath one turns 'a fresh clone has no gate' from silent to red, and it is the natural home for gate-guards-1's `allowOnly: false` so a later 'tidy' cannot remove it. Keep it to the four assertions above — a longer token list is churn.

candidates.pattern: The gate's input must be the artifact being committed: refuse a partially staged commit rather than test the working tree and stamp the index
candidates.failurePrevented: `git add -p`, or editing a file after `git add`, then `git commit`: the hook runs `npx vitest run` over the WORKING tree, goes green, and git records the INDEX — content nobody tested. A build input the gate never looked at, JCLAW-1178's shape ("an edit ships nothing while the gate reports up to date").
candidates.jclawEvidence: test/SpaBuildInputsConformanceTest.java:19-23 "A build input outside those roots is invisible to it, so an edit ships nothing while the gate reports 'up to date': the guide's markdown was exactly that until JCLAW-1178."; AGENTS.md:83 the pre-commit uses `lint-staged` (staged-file scoped) for the frontend.
candidates.builtAndExercised: JClaw: commits 47c9529c and 4ae46865 2026-09-09 (JCLAW-1178/1179), the conformance test reads the gate's roots FROM the script (`GATE_ROOTS_LINE` over jclaw.sh:2936 `ls-files -z -- frontend docs/user-guide`). The staged-vs-tree analogue on our side is INFERENCE — no incident in our logs; I did not find evidence it has bitten.
candidates.ourEvidence: .githooks/pre-commit:21 `STAGED=$(git diff --cached --name-only)` is used only for the docs-only decision; :28-43 `run_step` runs `sh -c "$2"` against the tree with no `git stash` and no staged-vs-unstaged comparison. The docs-only path itself is SAFE: `grep -rnE 'readFileSync\([^)]*\.(md)' tests scripts .claude` → only tests/ledgerEvidence.test.ts:125 (a temp-dir fixture), so no `.md` under git is a gate input (330 tracked .md files, none read by a test or gate).
candidates.proposal:
.githooks/pre-commit, after STAGED (4 lines): `PARTIAL=$(git diff --name-only | grep -Fxf <(printf '%s
' "$STAGED"))`; `if [ -n "$PARTIAL" ]; then printf '❌ partially staged — the gate would test a tree you are not committing:
%s
' "$PARTIAL"; exit 1; fi`. Refuse, never auto-stash (a stash inside a hook is the non-idempotent-replay killer in miniature).
candidates.doneCriterion: Edit a .ts file, `git add` it, edit it again, `git commit` → refused naming the file; `git add` again → the gate runs.
candidates.cost: 4 lines of sh; ~10 min. Note: `<(...)` needs bash, and the hook is `#!/bin/sh` — use a temp file or `grep -Fx -f` on a here-string alternative; keep it POSIX.
candidates.why: Cheap and fail-closed, but ranked last: solo workflow is mostly `git add -A`, and there is no evidence it has bitten. Take it only if gate-guards-5 is being written anyway; skip otherwise under 'simplest change wins'.

antiPatterns.what: Treating every file named '*Conformance*' as a gate-guard. SkillConformanceServiceConformTest is a plain unit test of a service that happens to be called SkillConformanceService — it guards no gate.
antiPatterns.evidence: test/SkillConformanceServiceConformTest.java:19-24 "Coverage for SkillConformanceService#conform's offline failure paths and the applyHardGates edges ... missing SKILL.md, LLM-unresolvable". Nothing in it reads a build file, a runner rule or a scan floor.
antiPatterns.whyNotForUs: Do not budget a 'port' for it; there is nothing to port. Listed so the parent does not count it as a ninth pattern.

antiPatterns.what: Guarding a checker with a NEGATIVE string blacklist over the build script (`script.contains("excludedPaths")`, `disable("NullAway")`, `-XepDisableAllChecks`, ...). Any new spelling of 'off' passes; any mention of a listed token inside a string or a differently-purposed option fails.
antiPatterns.evidence: test/NullnessGateConformanceTest.java:35-37 SILENT_SWITCH_OFFS = 7 literal strings; :71-73 `assertFalse(script.contains(off), ...)` — and 88b142ee shows the list was only assembled after the first version missed them, i.e. it enumerates yesterday's bypasses.
antiPatterns.whyNotForUs: Our existing guards are structural, not lexical: config-purity RESOLVES every import target (tests/config-purity.test.ts:37-48) and self-tests the scanner against 16 caught + 4 clean fixtures; claimcheck SPLITS code from comment with a scanner (claimcheckLib.ts:121-177) rather than regex-stripping. For gate-guards-5 assert the POSITIVE tokens with comments stripped and stop; do not import the blacklist.

antiPatterns.what: Hand-typed count floors and pins that no test cross-reads (`examined > 400`, `KNOWN_ESCAPING_IMPORTS = 14`, `KNOWN_MANAGERS = 7`, `scanned.size() >= 7`, `acquirers >= 20`) — five numbers in four files, each a separate copy of a fact about the tree.
antiPatterns.evidence: test/TestDiscoveryConformanceTest.java:64, test/SpaBuildInputsConformanceTest.java:39, test/SidecarDefaultPortsConformanceTest.java:29, test/ResourceLeakGateConformanceTest.java:95 and :131. The SpaBuildInputs comment even states the exact figure ("fourteen markdown files") as a floor, so the day a fifteenth is added the doc-comment is stale while the test stays green.
antiPatterns.whyNotForUs: We already do the stronger thing where exactness matters — chaosGate reads `EXPECTED_TOTAL` out of the runner (tests/chaosGate.test.ts:70-75) and configTwins pins 36 with the enumeration named — and we use floors only where an exact pin would churn (claimcheck.test.ts:327-336, "well under the measured 1,703 / 401"). Keep that split; do not import scattered floors.

antiPatterns.what: Running the gate-guards only inside a 5-8 minute suite that is invoked at pre-push/CI, so a switched-off checker is discovered a push later.
antiPatterns.evidence: AGENTS.md:30 "the full suite is 5–8 min"; :37 "Pre-push runs a wildcard-import grep, spotlessCheck and compileJava before the suite"; NullnessGateConformanceTest.java:22 "fail a test run rather than a later push" — the guard's own stated ambition is 'a test run', which for JClaw is minutes, not seconds.
antiPatterns.whyNotForUs: Our guards sit in a sub-second pre-commit (claimcheck ~0.2 s per CLAUDE.md; chaosGate resolves 43 anchors without applying one). Every candidate above is placed in pre-commit or in the hook itself; none should be moved to a slice gate or a later stage.

antiPatterns.what: Proving a guard works with a unit test of its predicate only (`thePredicateNamesTheShapeItIsLookingFor`) and never planting the failure in the real tree.
antiPatterns.evidence: test/TestDiscoveryConformanceTest.java:69-91 exercises `declaresUnreachableTests` on string fixtures; `grep -rn 'plant' test/*Conformance*.java` finds no plant harness, and none of the eight files is exercised by disarming the guard it protects. (Inference from the eight files and AGENTS.md read; I did not search JClaw's whole tree for a chaos runner.)
antiPatterns.whyNotForUs: Our standing rule is 'chaos-test every guard: plant the failure, watch red' (SSHD CLAUDE.md), and the harness ships 33 plants against its own runner (agent-harness/harness/plants/*.plants.mjs, README.md:131 "33 plants, all RED"). Each candidate above carries a by-hand red/green in its done-criterion; do not accept a predicate-only self-test as proof.
